claims.text: II.1: "Begin the morning by saying to thyself, I shall meet with the busybody, the ungrateful, arrogant, deceitful, envious, unsocial. All these things happen to them by reason of their ignorance of what is good and evil." và "For we are made for co-operation, like feet, like hands, like eyelids, like the rows of the upper and lower teeth." (Long)

sources.quote: BEGIN the morning by saying to thyself, I shall meet with the busybody, the ungrateful, arrogant, deceitful, envious, unsocial. All these things happen to them by reason of their ignorance of what is good and evil.
sources.where: II.1; câu sau trong cùng mục: "For we are made for co-operation, like feet, like hands, like eyelids, like the rows of the upper and lower teeth."

claims.text: Bản dịch của Logos của II.1 (kẻ tọc mạch ... vì họ không biết đâu là thiện, đâu là ác; sinh ra để hợp tác)

sources.quote: ignorance of what is good and evil

claims.text: VII.26: khi ai làm hại mình, xét họ hành động theo quan niệm nào về thiện ác; thấy rồi sẽ thương họ, không ngạc nhiên cũng không giận

sources.quote: 26. When a man has done thee any wrong, immediately consider with what opinion about good or evil he has done wrong. For when thou hast seen this, thou wilt pity him, and wilt neither wonder nor be angry.

claims.text: VIII.47: "If thou art pained by any external thing, it is not this thing that disturbs thee, but thy own judgment about it. And it is in thy power to wipe out this judgment now." và "...why dost thou not rather act than complain?"

sources.quote: 47. If thou art pained by any external thing, it is not this thing that disturbs thee, but thy own judgment about it. And it is in thy power to wipe out this judgment now.
sources.where: VIII.47; "why dost thou not rather act than complain?" cùng mục

claims.text: Bản dịch của Logos của VIII.47 sát nghĩa; nhận xét câu thứ hai trả lời trường hợp khổ vì chưa làm một điều đúng

sources.quote: even if thou art pained because thou art not doing some particular thing which seems to thee to be right, why dost thou not rather act than complain?

claims.text: II.11: "Since it is possible that thou mayest depart from life this very moment, regulate every act and thought accordingly."

sources.quote: 11. Since it is possible[3] that thou mayest depart from life this very moment, regulate every act and thought accordingly.

claims.text: IV.48: "Pass then through this little space of time conformably to nature, and end thy journey in content, as an olive falls off when it is ripe, blessing nature who produced it, and thanking the tree on which it grew."

sources.quote: Pass then through this little space of time conformably to nature, and end thy journey in content, as an olive falls off when it is ripe, blessing nature who produced it, and thanking the tree on which it grew.

claims.text: VII.69: đức hạnh hoàn hảo là sống mỗi ngày như ngày cuối, không cuồng loạn, không uể oải, không giả dối

sources.quote: 69. The perfection of moral character consists in this, in passing every day as the last, and in being neither violently excited nor torpid nor playing the hypocrite.

claims.text: IX.30: "Look down from above on the countless herds of men and their countless solemnities, and the infinitely varied voyagings in storms and calms, and the differences among those who are born, who live together, and die."; mục kết thúc với: bao người không biết tên ta, sẽ sớm quên, danh tiếng sau khi chết chẳng có giá trị

sources.quote: 30. Look down from above on the countless herds of men and their countless solemnities, and the infinitely varied voyagings in storms and calms, and the differences among those who are born, who live together, and die.
sources.where: IX.30; cuối mục: "how many know not even thy name, and how many will soon forget it ... neither a posthumous name is of any value"

claims.text: VII.48: Marcus ghi ý nhìn việc dưới đất như từ một chỗ cao là "một câu hay của Platon"

sources.quote: 48. This is a fine saying of Plato:[12] That he who is discoursing about men should look also at earthly things as if he viewed them from some higher place

claims.text: X.28: "Imagine every man who is grieved at anything or discontented to be like a pig which is sacrificed and kicks and screams." và "...only to the rational animal is it given to follow voluntarily what happens; but simply to follow is a necessity imposed on all."

sources.quote: 28. Imagine every man who is grieved at anything or discontented to be like a pig which is sacrificed and kicks and screams.
sources.where: X.28; câu sau nằm ở đoạn thứ hai của cùng mục: "only to the rational animal is it given to follow voluntarily what happens; but simply to follow is a necessity imposed on all."

claims.text: IV.3: Marcus đặt câu hỏi thiên ý hay nguyên tử, "dù vũ trụ có thiên ý hay chỉ là nguyên tử" (dòng cuối đoạn 5)

sources.quote: either there is providence or atoms [fortuitous concurrence of things]
Nine times in the Meditations, Marcus lays out the alternatives: providence, nature, reason, on the one hand, or atoms, on the other (iv.3, vi.24, vii.32 ...)

claims.text: Dù vũ trụ có thiên ý hay chỉ là nguyên tử, oán trách điều đã xảy ra cũng chẳng ích gì (IV.3)
claims.fix: ... oán trách điều đã xảy ra cũng chẳng ích gì (VIII.17; xem thêm IV.3)

sources.quote: whom dost thou blame,—the atoms [chance] or the gods? Both are foolish. Thou must blame nobody.
sources.where: VIII.17: câu kết luận "đừng oán trách dù vì nguyên tử hay thần" nằm ở VIII.17 (SEP cũng dẫn viii.17, ix.39); IV.3 chỉ nêu hai khả năng để giải tỏa bất mãn

sources.quote: if the way things are is due to providence, then they could not be better and one is wrong to grumble, but if the way things are is due to chance, then it is pointless to grumble (viii.17, ix.39).

notes:
Lỗi nhe: dẫn vị trí cho kết luận "oán trách vô ích dù thiên ý hay nguyên tử" nên là VIII.17 (xem cả ở mục Tái dựng, P3). IV.3 vẫn đặt đúng cặp thiên ý-nguyên tử trong ngữ cảnh bất mãn. Không phải lỗi vừa/nghiêm trọng.
Lượt 2: bài đã sửa vị trí thành "(VIII.17; xem thêm IV.3)" đúng fix; đối chiếu lại Wikisource Book VIII §17 ("whom dost thou blame,—the atoms [chance] or the gods? Both are foolish"); fixed: true.
